measure.measure_definition: Occurrence: participant meets clinical remission per Adapted Mayo score at Week 8.; Participants; Adapted Mayo score ranges 0 to 9 with higher scores representing more severe disease; it includes stool frequency subscore (SFS), rectal bleeding subscore (RBS), and endoscopic subscore. Non-responder imputation incorporating multiple imputation to handle missing data due to COVID-19 was used.; Clinical remission is defined as an Adapted Mayo score ≤ 2, with SFS ≤ 1 and not higher than Baseline, RBS of 0, and endoscopic subscore ≤ 1.
measure.measure_name: Clinical remission per Adapted Mayo score

measure.measure_definition: Occurrence: participant meets clinical response per Adapted Mayo score at Week 8.; Participants; Adapted Mayo score ranges 0 to 9, composed of SFS (0-3), RBS (0-3), and endoscopic subscore (0-3); higher scores represent more severe disease. Non-responder imputation incorporating multiple imputation to handle missing data due to COVID-19 was used.; Clinical response per the Adapted Mayo Score is defined as a decrease in Adapted Mayo score ≥ 2 points and ≥ 30% from Baseline, plus a decrease in RBS ≥ 1 or an absolute RBS ≤ 1.
measure.measure_name: Clinical response per Adapted Mayo score

measure.measure_definition: Occurrence: participant meets endoscopic improvement at Week 8.; Participants; Endoscopies were assessed by a blinded central reader and scored according to the endoscopic subscore: 0 = normal or inactive disease; 1 = mild disease (erythema, decreased vascular pattern); 2 = moderate disease (marked erythema, lack of vascular pattern, any friability, erosions); 3 = severe disease (spontaneous bleeding, ulceration). Non-responder imputation incorporating multiple imputation to handle missing data due to COVID-19 was used.; Endoscopic improvement is defined as an endoscopic subscore of 0 or 1.

Moderately to severely active UC was defined by adapted Mayo score 5–9 and endoscopy subscore 2–3 confirmed by a central reader.
